description: A light, soft, pale cream to straw-colored hardwood that is easy to cut and carve. Widely used for model making, sauna benches and panelling, mouldings, picture frames, and as a core or veneer wood.

hazards.summary: Obeche is one of the best documented wood causes of allergic occupational asthma. Many workers have been confirmed by bronchial challenge plus skin or IgE tests, including a Finnish series in which 27 of 34 symptomatic workers had a positive challenge.
Hives where the wood or dust touches the skin have been confirmed in obeche-allergic workers with rubbing tests and specific IgE. People with obeche asthma may also react through the skin.
HSE lists skin irritation, nettle rash, and dermatitis from handling obeche articles.
HSE also lists irritation of the airways, sneezing, wheezing, and feeling feverish among reported effects of obeche dust.
IARC classifies all wood dust as carcinogenic to humans, chiefly through cancers of the nose and sinuses. This applies to obeche dust as it does to any other wood.

known_compounds.name: Trip s 1 (38 kDa class I chitinase)
thaumatin-like protein (24 kDa) and gamma-expansin (12 kDa)
known_compounds.role: protein allergens recognized by symptomatic workers

related_species_note: Cross-reactivity has been shown between obeche and ramin (Hinojosa-1986) and with natural rubber latex (Venturini-2004, Kespohl-2005). One obeche-allergic carpenter had anaphylaxis to tamarillo fruit (Vidal-2006). Obeche from Cameroon (ayous) was found to contain less of the major allergen than obeche from Ghana (wawa) (Kespohl-2008).
image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed obeche (Triplochiton scleroxylon) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Pale creamy white to light straw-yellow throughout, with little difference between heartwood and sapwood. Interlocked grain giving a faint ribbon stripe, moderately coarse open texture with visible pores, and a soft low luster. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.
image_alt: Planed board of obeche with pale creamy-yellow wood and a faint ribbon stripe from interlocked grain.
notes_internal: Trip s 1 primary characterization is Kespohl-2005 (Allergy 2005;60:808-814). Baatjies-2023 and Schlunssen-2018 not cited because primaries were reachable. Quirce-2000 (PMID 10932087, J Allergy Clin Immunol 106:400-1, obeche allergens) and Krawczyk-Szulc-2014 (PMID 24840887, SIC-confirmed) also support level 1 but were not added to keep the list short; can be added. Hinojosa papers call obeche 'African maple' - it is not a maple.
